claims.text: Hari Kota posted The Full AI Governance Stack on LinkedIn, ten layers and forty-six examples under the line most teams cover only 4 or 5, and asked how the owner would structure the graph across the layers.
claims.quote: How would you structure the graph across the layers?

claims.text: Rather than describe the answer the owner built it: the AI Governance Graph vault opens as an app with its read key published, and everything in the article is a view of it.
claims.quote: This is my take, and rather than describe it I built it.

claims.text: Hari's table is kept exactly as posted, every cell a node, and the release gate checks eighty-five nodes byte for byte against the transcription: ten layers, ten purposes, forty-six examples, the title, subtitle, footer and claims.
claims.quote: ten layers, ten purposes, forty-six examples, the title, the subtitle, the footer and the post's claims, eighty-five nodes in all

claims.text: The post's claims the graph tests are that the gaps show up in layers 3, 5 and 10, and the test: pick one AI system and name the owner and the risk tier.
claims.quote: pick one AI system in your company and name the owner and the risk tier

claims.text: Read as a graph, the table already holds ten edges across layers: the EU AI Act in rows 2, 6 and 10, ISO/IEC 42001 in 4 and 10, the NIST AI RMF in 4 and 6, and Singapore in 3 and 8.
claims.quote: Ten edges, and none of them is ours.

claims.text: Each layer is its own world with its own ontology in its owners' vocabulary; none is asked to fit the others, and they share only the grammar.
claims.quote: None of those worlds is asked to fit the others.

claims.text: The shared grammar is five rules: every edge a verb with its inverse, relates_to banned, properties carry data not meaning, supersede never delete, render the answer not the graph; the vault has ninety-one verbs.
claims.quote: The vault has ninety-one verbs, each with its inverse, in one file.

claims.text: The edges between worlds come from the provisions themselves: Article 26(2) of the EU AI Act joins binding law to people, and GOVERN 1.6 of the NIST AI RMF joins a framework to the inventory.
claims.quote: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.

claims.text: Article 4 on AI literacy was replaced in July 2026 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, and the 2024 wording stays in the graph, struck through.
claims.quote: The 2024 wording stays in the graph, struck through.

claims.text: The knowledge graph has 329 edges, 140 of them between layers: ten from Hari's table, eleven from what his labels name, and 119 of the newsroom's, each citing the fact it rests on and marked as an addition.
claims.quote: Counted, the knowledge graph has 329 edges, 140 of them between layers

claims.text: Per instrument the EU AI Act's articles reach nine of the ten layers, as do ISO/IEC 42001's clauses, and the NIST AI RMF reaches eight, which is the argument for a graph in a single row of a table.
claims.quote: its articles reach nine of the ten layers, as do ISO/IEC 42001's clauses; the NIST AI RMF reaches eight

value.unit: layers reached by the EU AI Act

claims.text: The zoom from a cell goes to the instrument, its provisions and an organisation, with a breadcrumb back; the instrument is detailed in the Regulation Graph vault, which is what fractal means in practice.
claims.quote: a node in one graph is a whole graph somewhere else, with its own vocabulary, reachable by a named edge

claims.text: Several of Hari's examples moved in 2026: the EU AI Act amended from 27 July, Colorado SB 26-189 signed 14 May, and promptfoo joining OpenAI in March; a table is correct on the day it is drawn, a graph keeps time.
claims.quote: A table is correct on the day it is drawn.

claims.text: Hari's do this today test is a query in disguise: follow is_owned_by to a person and is_classified_in to a tier with its basis, and if either path ends early that is the gap.
claims.quote: Hari's test is the best line in the post, because it is a query in disguise

claims.text: On the fictional Hollow Oak Home, eight systems in three jurisdictions, five pass; the fraud score has an owner and no tier, the demand forecast a tier and no owner, and the transcription tool bought on a company card neither.
claims.quote: Five of the eight systems pass: an owner and a tier with its basis.

value.unit: systems passing the do this today test

claims.text: The CV screening assistant passes the first test, yet walked across ten layers three rows come back red: no literacy or competence record for the HR Lead, and a bias test whose result no report receives.
claims.quote: Hari's test is the right first question.

claims.text: Hari's three gaps become queries with results on the shop: Singapore soft law that no role tracks, the transcription tool missing from the register, and the HR Lead owning a high-risk system with no training record.
claims.quote: Each of the gaps Hari names becomes a query with a plain question, a traversal written out step by step, and a result

claims.text: Most teams cover only 4 or 5 splits into three questions: ten of ten layers have a complete path for some system, one of ten is complete for every registered system, and none once the expenses tool is counted.
claims.quote: A layer can be covered somewhere and almost nowhere, and a stack has no way to show the difference.

value.unit: layers complete for every registered system

claims.text: The bring-your-own view runs the test and the gap queries in the browser on two pasted CSV files of systems and people; nothing is sent anywhere and the vault is never written.
claims.quote: Nothing is sent anywhere and the vault is never written.

claims.text: One model script writes every data file, 335 nodes and 702 edges with one ontology per layer; facts come from a research pack of 114 entries dated 9 October 2026, and a release gate of twenty-two checks reproduces every file.
claims.quote: One model script writes every data file: 335 nodes, 702 edges, one ontology per layer

value.unit: edges written by the model script

claims.text: It is a method and a worked example: Hollow Oak Home is fictional, nothing says any real organisation complies, tools are named only as examples of Hari's layers, and it is not legal advice.
claims.quote: Hollow Oak Home is fictional.

claims.text: Where a primary site refused automated access, the fact is shown with an unverified badge rather than presented as checked.
claims.quote: the fact is shown with an unverified badge rather than presented as checked

claims.text: The idea is not new: Hernandez, Golpayegani and Lewis proposed a knowledge graph mapping the EU AI Act to standards in 2024, AIRO and the W3C DPV AI extension give vocabularies, and NIST's crosswalks are published edges; the vault adds the fractal shape.
claims.quote: What the vault adds is the fractal shape

claims.text: The EU AI Act itself is a graph in the Regulation Graph vault, parsed from the official XML article by article, and the AI BCF as a graph is another open vault.
claims.quote: parsed from the official XML, article by article

claims.text: The article was researched, built and written by agent@riskmandate.ai running Claude Opus 5.5 for Dinis Cruz, from the LinkedIn comment thread, with facts checked on 9 October 2026.
claims.quote: Facts checked on 9 October 2026 against primary sources where they could be reached; not legal advice.
